# Agentic Engineering Protocol (dinostack)

This project uses the DinoStack agentic engineering methodology. The protocol body is
trigger-loaded via the `dinostack` skill - it does not load unconditionally from this file.

**Note:** This file is auto-generated by `.gemini/build.sh`. Do not edit it directly.

## Loading the methodology

Invoke the `dinostack` skill (`activate_skill`) before any software development work:
implementing features, fixing bugs, reviewing or refactoring code, debugging, testing,
deploying, working with agents or subagents, making architecture decisions, setting up
projects, managing dependencies, writing scripts, or any task that involves reading,
writing, or reasoning about code and systems. The skill lives at
`.gemini/skills/dinostack/SKILL.md` (project-local) or `~/.gemini/skills/dinostack/SKILL.md`
(installed globally) - the minimal corpus, with a "Deferred at this corpus" pointer block
naming any deferred rule's trigger. If a named trigger fires, read
`.gemini/skills/dinostack/SKILL.full.md` (or the `~/.gemini/` global copy) for the full,
unfiltered text.

**Activation preflight:** before doing implementation work in a project, check whether
agentic engineering is active there. See the "Activation preflight" section (§01) inside
the `dinostack` skill body once loaded.

**Known limitation - headless/non-interactive runs:** Gemini CLI denies `activate_skill` by
default outside an interactive session (see `.gemini/README.md` §Trigger-loaded methodology
(DS-184), "Known limitation" paragraph, for the full explanation and both override routes).
A scripted, non-interactive Gemini run will get neither this stub's full body nor the skill
unless the operator has explicitly opted in to one of those overrides.

## Protocol Reference

For detailed protocol specs, see the reference docs:

- `skeptic-protocol.md` - Skeptic loop orchestration, findings classification, sign-off format
- `subagent-protocol.md` - Parallel spawning rules, worktree isolation, task decomposition
- `agent-team.md` - Named agent roles, composed flows, decision rules
- `design-goals.md` - System design principles and goals

These live in `.gemini/references/` (local copies in this repo) or `~/.gemini/references/` after install.

For command templates (skeptic, implement-ticket, wrap, etc.), see `.gemini/commands/`.
